newsitem.title: USA: Tight world cotton supplies next five years - ICAC.
newsitem.headline: Tight world cotton supplies next five years - ICAC.

text.p: World cotton supplies will be tight for the next five years and prices would average between 80 cents and 90 cents per pound through the 2002-2003 season, the International Cotton Advisory Council (ICAC) said.
China was forecast "to remain a significant net importer," the council said in a monthly report prepared for release Monday.

For 1997-98, the council forecast production of 19.43 million tonnes, up 320,000 tonnes from 1996-97 but accompanied by higher use and minimal stocks building. Average prices were pegged at 81 cents in 1996-97 and 83 cents in 1997-98. Since 1973-74, the average price has been 74 cents.

"The outlook for cotton supply and use over the next five seasons is characterized by slow growth in production, a tightening of stocks relative to use outside China ... and growth in world consumption limited by higher prices," the report said.
Insects, disease, economic difficulties and change in government policy were expected to constrain yield growth.
China's cotton imports were expected to fall by 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes in 1997-98 but tight stocks would keep prices strong, the council said.
